Kingdom of Kelantan also known as Kalantan and Kingdom of Chermin was a Islam kingdom (formely Hindu-Buddhist) located on Kelantan under Chermin Dynasty rule
History
establishment
Kingdom of Kelantan started when Chermin Dynasty founded by Raja Bharubhasa in late 1336. Kelantan formely was under Langkasuka Kingdom, ruled by Jawaka Dynasty, following id decline of Langkasuka Kingdom, Raja Bharubhasa as the heir of Jawaka Dynasty start a new kingdom on Kelantan known as Kingdom of Kelantan and sometimes also known as Kingdom of Chermin.
Capital to Bukit Banau
Capital city of Kelantan originally was on Kota Mahligai but because of Siamese threat, King Bharubhasa retreat to Bukit Panau in middle of Kelantan
Islamization
during early reign era of Raja Bharubhasa, he convert to Islam and changed name to Mahmud Shah ibni Abdullah. By mid-14 century nickname Jiddah Riayah Saadatussalam was given to Kingdom of Kelantan by Arabs and Champa traders.
Malacca invansion
during Sultan Mansur Shah reign, Kelantan was attacked by Melakan troops commanded by Sultan Mahmud Shah. Kota Kelantan being attacked by Melakan troops then Sultan Mansur son Raja Gembuk escaped from Melakan troops but Sultan Mansur Daughters, Onang Kinang, Onang Jupa and Onang Jubak was captured by Melakan troops and Melakan troops bring them to Sultan Mahmud Shah. Onang Kinang was forced to marry Sultan Mahmud Shah.
Majapahit II
During Sultan Iskandar Shah in 1432, he marry a Javanese princess and proclaiming Kelantan Kingdom as Western Majapahit or also known as Second Majapahit (Majapahit II). He moved back capital city to kota mahligai.
Majapahit II ended after Siamese invansion in 1467

The Chermin Dynasty utilized a centralized administrative system that blended Islamic governance with the Majapahit Mandala model. The Sultan was supported by a hierarchy of ministers, including the Bendahara and the Syahbandar, the latter of whom managed the kingdom's vital maritime trade. Administration was decentralized through provincial lords, while the legal system increasingly integrated Sharia principles alongside Malay tradition
